paper.title: Combinatorial Pure Exploration with Full-Bandit or Partial Linear Feedback

settings.name_in_paper: Combinatorial pure exploration with full-bandit linear feedback (CPE-BL)
unmapped: Full-bandit feedback on a combinatorial action: only the sum x^T(theta+eta_t) is observed
Noise is a zero-mean vector eta_t in [-1,1]^d added per base arm
settings.definition_quote: At each time step $t$, a learner pulls a super arm $x_t$ and receives a random reward (full-bandit feedback)  $y_t=x^{\top} (\theta + \eta_t )$, where $\eta_t$ is a zero-mean noise vector bounded in $[-1,1]^d$ ... $\| \theta\|_2 \leq L$ ... we assume that the optimal $x^*$ is unique

settings.name_in_paper: Combinatorial pure exploration with partial linear feedback (CPE-PL)
unmapped: Feedback y_t = M_{x_t}(theta+eta_t) with known transformation matrices M_x
Expected reward rbar(x,theta) possibly nonlinear and not directly observed; L_p-Lipschitz in theta (Assumption 1)
Existence of a known global observer set sigma with M_sigma of full column rank (Assumption 2)
Learner knows global observer set sigma, constant beta_sigma and Lipschitz constant L_p
settings.definition_quote: In CPE-PL, each super arm $x \in \mathcal{X}$ is associated with a transformation matrix $M_x \in \mathbb{R}^{m_x \times d}$ ... a learner pulls a super arm $x_t$ and observes a random linear feedback  vector $y_t=M_{x_t} (\theta + \eta_t )$ ... the learner gains a random reward with expectation of $\bar{r}(x_t, \theta)$.

settings.name_in_paper: CPE-BL, (epsilon,delta)-PAC identification with sub-Gaussian noise (CLUNCB analysis)
unmapped: Full-bandit feedback on a combinatorial action: only the sum of base-arm rewards is observed
settings.definition_quote: Suppose that a noise $\eta_t$ is $\kappa$-sub-Gaussian. If the $\ell_2$-norm of parameter $\theta$ is less than $L$ ...

bound.expression: Sum(c_0/Delta_sup(i)**2*(log(1/delta) + log(X_size) + log(log(1/Delta_sup(i)))), (i, 2, floor(d/2))) + c_0*d*(alpha_pa*sqrt(m) + alpha_pa**2)/Delta_sup(d + 1)**2*(log(1/delta) + log(X_size) + log(log(1/Delta_sup(d + 1))))

symbols.Delta_sup: Delta_sup(i): gap between the optimal super arm and the super arm with the i-th largest expected reward

conditions: efficient maximization oracle over X (Lawler's k-best procedure)

source.label: thm:CPE-BL
source.quote: With probability at least $1-\delta$, the \textsf{PolyALBA} algorithm (Algorithm \ref{alg:PolyALBA}) returns the best super arm $x^*$ with sample complexity O( \sum_{i=2}^{\lfloor d/2 \rfloor} \frac{c_0}{\Delta_i^2} (\ln \delta^{-1} + \ln |\mathcal{X}|+\ln\ln \Delta_i^{-1}) + \frac{c_0 d (\alpha \sqrt{m} + \alpha^2 )}{\Delta_{d+1}^2} (...)), where $\alpha = \sqrt{md/\xi_{\min}(\widetilde{M}(\lambda^*_{\mathcal{X}_{\sigma}}))}$.

results.notes: Delta_i is gap of i-th best super arm (not base arm). alpha is algorithm-computed quantity.

bound.expression: Sum(c_0/Delta_sup(i)**2*(log(1/delta) + log(X_size) + log(log(1/Delta_sup(i)))), (i, 2, floor(d/2))) + c_0*d*(alpha_pa*sqrt(m) + alpha_pa**2)/Delta_sup(d + 1)**2*(log(1/delta) + log(X_size) + log(log(1/Delta_sup(d + 1))))

symbols.Delta_sup: gap of i-th best super arm
symbols.alpha_pa: min{nu*/sqrt(d), min_i sqrt(m d/xi_min(Mtilde(lambda_i)))}, nu* optimal value of LP_primal in Algorithm (ellipsoid method)

conditions: X admits efficient separation oracle for its polytope (e.g. matroid, matroid intersection, s-t paths)
tuning: distribution lambda computed by the ellipsoid-method approximation of G-optimal design

source.label: corollary:ellipsoid_method
source.quote: Let $\nu^*$ be the optimal value for $\mathrm{LP}_{\mathrm{primal}}$ obtained in Algorithm~\ref{alg:G-opt-approx}. With probability at least $1-\delta$, the \textsf{PolyALBA} algorithm will return the best super arm $x^*$ with the expected sample complexity O(...), where $\alpha =\min\{ \frac{\nu^*}{\sqrt{d}}, \min_{i \in [n]}\sqrt{\frac{md}{\xi_{\min}(\tilde{M}(\lambda_i))}} \}$.

results.notes: Stated as 'expected sample complexity' with probability 1-delta; mix of expectation (over random choice of lambda) and high probability. Same form as Theorem with a different alpha.

symbols.sigma_size: |sigma|, size of the global observer set (<= d)
symbols.beta_sigma: max over eta in [-1,1]^d of ||(M_sigma^T M_sigma)^{-1} sum_i M_{x_i}^T M_{x_i} eta_i||_2
symbols.L_p: Lipschitz constant of expected reward rbar(x,theta) in theta (Assumption 1)

conditions: Assumption 1: rbar(x,.) is L_p-Lipschitz in theta
Assumption 2: a global observer set with full-column-rank M_sigma exists
polynomial-time offline maximization oracle for rbar

source.label: thm:GCB_ub
source.quote: With probability at least $1-\delta$, the \textsf{GCB-PE} algorithm (Algorithm \ref{alg:GCB-PE}) will return the optimal super arm $x^*$ with sample complexity $O ( \frac{|\sigma| \beta_\sigma^2 L_p^2}{\Delta_{\textup{min}}^2} \log ( \frac{ \beta_\sigma^2 L_p^2}{\Delta_{\textup{min}}^2 \delta } ) ) $, where $|\sigma| \leq d$.

results.notes: Delta_min is the smallest gap in expected reward rbar between optimal and other super arms. Proof gives explicit constant 655. For linear reward L_p = sqrt(m).

symbols.H_tilde: max_e M(lambda_C)^{-1}(e,e) * min{9 width(X)^2/Delta_e^2, 4 m^2/(epsilon d^2)}, lambda_C = empirical pull distribution of CLUNCB, Delta_e = base-arm gap as in Chen et al. 2014

conditions: T sufficiently large so that A_T/T approximates M(lambda_C)

source.label: Corollary:CLUCB
source.quote: Let $\lambda_{\mathrm{C}} \in \triangle(\cX)$ be a distribution in which $\lambda_{\mathrm{C}}(x)$ represents the ratio that $x$ is pulled by \textsf{CLUNCB}. results.notes: Paper's kappa is sub-Gaussian parameter (mapped to sigma), iota the ridge parameter (lam). Bound depends on algorithm's own allocation lambda_C and the proof uses an approximation step; (epsilon,delta)-PAC with prob >= 1-delta.
